utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84bis-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj, Idriz Balaj, and Lahi Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have appearances for the day, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. For the Prosecution Daniela Kravetz, together with Aditya Menon, Andrej Micovic, and our case manager Line Pedersen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And for Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Ben Emmerson for Ramush Haradinaj, together with Rodney Dixon, Annie O'Reilly, and Andrew Strong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Emmerson. For Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, Gregor Guy-Smith, together with Colleen Rohan, Chad Mair, Holly Buchanan, Gentian Zyberi, and our intern William Fife [overlapping speakers] Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And for Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Richard Harvey for Mr. Brahimaj, assisted by Mr. Paul Troop and Mr. Luke Boenisch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Harvey. May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, sir. How are you -- how do you feel today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You feel okay? If you don't feel well, please do indicate to us so that we can do something. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Don't hesitate to mention it when you don't feel well. Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday when we left off we were talking about your first visit to the village of Jabllanice, and specifically we were talking about when a Serb young boy -- man and two Roma boys were taken out of the house that you visited to a yard. Do you remember we were talking about that?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, when the Serb young man and the two Roma boys were taken out to the yard, who was present in the yard?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there, my comrade who was with me, Maxhup, Idriz Gashi, and another, a villager of theirs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And where in the yard were these three young men taken to?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right outside the door of the house. They were a metre and a half or 2 metres away from that door.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Would this be in the front of the house, the back of the house, or where exactly were they?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the house.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the Prosecutor move closer to the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, what happened to these three young men when they were taken out to the yard?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After 10 or 15 minutes, roughly, when we were all outside already, Mr. Ramush Haradinaj appeared, who was the main commander of the Dukagjini Zone at the time and Toger came too. Ramush wasn't really well, and that was the first occasion when I met him as commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Had you met him before that occasion? I'm speaking about Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was born in Germany, lived in Switzerland, and the gentleman also worked in Switzerland as a -- as a seasonal worker, and that's where I first met him but not as a commander but as a seasonal worker as all the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say "the gentleman," just so we're clear, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how much time before this occasion, when you saw him in Jabllanice, had you met this man, Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two years more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And other than having met him when both of you worked as seasonal workers, had you had any other encounter with him prior to this meeting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you, madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I had asked you, other than having met Mr. Haradinaj when both of you worked as seasonal workers, had you had any other opportunity to meet him prior to seeing him in Jabllanice? And, sir, can I just ask you to please wait until I turn off my microphone before you respond just because -- so the protective measures that are in place are effective. I see that you often try to respond immediately while I'm asking the question. So I'll just ask you to wait. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him in a cafe. There's an Albanian cafe in Switzerland, and that's a meeting-place for the workers there. And I met him there once.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You told us that you saw him arrive in this compound where you were in Jabllanice. What happened when he arrived?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember - and I'm saying that because it's been a long time - when he arrived we all had to salute him because he had a higher rank. After that, again to the best of my recollection, he called Maxhup "Teqe" and that's an expression of respect and they greeted each other. And then the interrogation began.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: May I stop you there before we move on to that. You also referred to a person known as Toger. Do you know that person's name?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Idriz Balaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just at that point, Madam Prosecutor, I also have something to clear. Sir, you indicated that when these two young Roma men were taken out into the yard, the people present there were yourself and your comrade and then Maxhup and Idriz Gashi and a villager. What I want to find out from you is where -- at that time where were the six people that you came with that you arrived with into this village? Because you -- so far you arrived into this house and you have now not told us anything about them. Where were they at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were around that house. They spoke to the villagers, and we were all there in one place. But they were not right next to me or next to them, but they were around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They also saw what was happening there? They were part of the group. They may not have stood next to you but they were -- were they part of the group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course they saw because they were all present. We weren't next to each other, but we were all in the same yard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it's correct to say that in addition to the people that you mentioned as present when these young men were taken out into the yard, we should also add those companions of yours that arrived with you in the village, six of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course because they were with me. They had arrived with me and we were all in that yard. As I have just said, we were not right next to each other, but we were all in the yard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about who was next to you. I'm asking you about what was present there, and the reason I'm asking you about these people is because you didn't mention them as present, sir. Okay? You can't tell me that everybody else that you have mentioned was right next to you, can you? Was Maxhup right next to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was near me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And was the villager next to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we were there together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, let me explain because I see -- we were all in the same yard, in the same yard, and I'm talking about a diameter of 3 to 4 metres, but not shoulder-to-shoulder. We were all near each other. Maxhup was near me, then my companion was also next to me and the others were standing around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And where were the six?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But that's what I'm explaining. They were standing there, standing around --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I've just one more question to clarify. Mr. Witness, you mentioned I think two times "my comrade," who was with you. Is that one of the six people or is that somebody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may, ma'am, I had said so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you -- I asked you who -- if you knew the name of the person that you referred to as Toger and you have said it was Idriz Balaj. Had you met Mr. Idriz Balaj before this occasion, when you saw him in Jabllanice at this compound?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how were you able to identify this person? How did you know who it was?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you go to meet somebody, they will introduce themselves as your hosts, and we were wearing the same uniforms. And it is normal for them to say who they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what did Idriz Balaj say when he introduced himself to you?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That his name was Idriz and that his nickname was Toger and that he was commander of a special unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did he mention which unit he was a commander of?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know which unit that was?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It was the Tigers. At that time they were mostly in the Dukagjini Zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how do you know this was the name of the unit?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any soldier who was there knew which unit was which and what it was called.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you've told us that Ramush Haradinaj arrived and that the soldiers there saluted him. What happened after he and Mr. Toger or Idriz Balaj arrived in this compound?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As usual, people greeted each other. And when he saw the two gypsies, he started to interrogate them, which is usual. He was asking them about where the Serb forces were, where the check-points were, and the like.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say "when he saw the two gypsies he started to interrogate them," whom are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Ramush Haradinaj, because it is a known fact that Ramush Haradinaj never liked the Roma. Even in Switzerland, in that cafe that I mentioned, he was known for that dislike of his, because they called him "Bace" in Albanian and entreated him not to kill them because they hadn't done anything, and he was probably irritated by that and he replied: "What do you mean 'Bace'? Tell me where the Serb troops are and where the check-points are."

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What does Bace mean?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bace means a man who you hold in esteem, who is a bit older, and whom you respect, and that's the meaning of that word.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say "they called him Bace," whom are you referring to by "they"?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the two Roma.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And whom were they calling "Bace"?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Just to go back a little bit, you told us that it was a known fact that Ramush Haradinaj never liked Roma -- the Roma. Where did you hear this or from whom did you hear this?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was something that one could hear. Ramush Haradinaj respected everybody and a close relative of mine, I needn't mention his name, was a member of his unit. And the two of us talked and the relative told me that he hates the Roma's guts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that. The interpreter missed your answer or part of your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that one relative of mine, a close relative, was a member of his unit. And since you asked me how I knew that he hated Roma, I explained to you that in the conversation between me and my relative, he told me that his commander hated the Roma, let alone the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if we could go into private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you told us that when Mr. Haradinaj saw the two gypsies, he started to interrogate them. Was anyone else -- did anyone else participate in this interrogation or was he the only one questioning the two Roma?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Toger and there was Maxhup.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What was Toger doing in this -- at the time?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Toger, because we were from two units, one from one zone and another from the other zone, and so he wanted to prove his value, he said at one point, "This is what you do to spies and enemies." He took a knife and cut his ear, just to show me that he was stronger than I or something of that kind, or that he was faithful to that special unit as a commander. He took a knife and cut the ear of one of the Roma.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what did Mr. -- the person you referred to as Maxhup, Mr. Brahimaj, do during this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the interrogation, Maxhup was also beating them up, as they were not willing to speak. He had this - how should I explain this to you? - a baseball bat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What was he -- what was Maxhup, or Lahi Brahimaj, doing with a baseball bat?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was hitting with the baseball bat, in order to extract as much information from them as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And whom was he hitting?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the Roma and the Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Where -- we'll start first with the Serb boy. Where was he hitting the boy, the Serb boy?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All over his body.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Was he the only one hitting the boy or did anyone else take part in this?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have rushed these questions and I wanted to relate this to you in more detail. I apologise. Well, before the interrogation started, at the point when I said that Ramush Haradinaj was asking them questions, on two or three occasions -- or he actually hit the man two or three times and he fell to the ground and they lifted him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say "he hit the man," which man are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking about the Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So just so we're clear, we're speaking about the Serbian boy. Are you saying that Ramush Haradinaj questioned this Serbian boy?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I did say, when he came - and I'll say the same thing again - when he arrived, the Roma started pleading with him, addressing him in that deferent way, and then he started asking them, "Well, where are your forces? Where are your tanks now?" And hit them once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say he hit them, are you referring to the Roma or the Serb boy or -- I'm just trying to understand, sir.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as I said a moment ago, I'm speaking about the Serb now. He asked the Serb, "Where are your Serbian forces, your tanks, your check-points?" So he hit him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did he also put those questions to the Romas, the two Roma boys?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very, very important, given the vacillation in this account, that Ms. Kravetz not ask a leading question of that kind and that's an extraordinarily direct leading question in circumstances where the witness's account is not coming out in a direct and coherent manner and one which I would not only object to but strongly object to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have any response to that, Madam Kravetz?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I don't think it's a leading question. I'm just trying to clarify the account. But we can start again and just have the witness tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection overruled. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I would like for you to tell what happened very clearly and we can take it point by point just so the Judges understand what you saw happening. Okay? So you say that you saw Mr. Ramush Haradinaj arrive in the compound. Can you tell us once again what happened after he and Mr. Balaj arrived in the compound? And I'm sorry, you may have to repeat yourself, but it's simply so we have it clear in the record.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you what I saw and how I saw it, the entire event. As I said, initially we got out, my comrade and I, and the rest were already out in the yard, including the prisoners, the two Roma and the Serb. Half an hour later perhaps, Ramush Haradinaj arrived with Toger. We said hello. Next started the interrogation. Where are your Serb forces, check-points, spies? The Roma started pleading with him, as I said, they were saying, "Don't kill us." He put one or two questions to the Serb, "Where are your check-points?" He was quite annoyed. The boy was so scared that he was unable to speak and he was tearful, and I felt that he hit him more out of the annoyance with him because he wouldn't speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say "he hit him," whom did he hit? And I'm just going to ask you -- just a second. Ask you tell your story just so it's clear, just to explain each time whether you're speaking about the Serbian boy or young man or one of the Roma, just so we understand. Okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you also mention with what he hit him?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I was going to get to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And also explain with what he hit him and who was doing the hitting, just so we understand. Okay? So you can explain that.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, Ramush Haradinaj asked the young Serb about where his forces were, their tanks, and such-like. The Serb was probably frightened, and that was the reason why he didn't answer these questions. And as I said, he punched him with his fist a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Now it's clear. What happened after Ramush Haradinaj punched the Serb boy a couple of times?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said and will repeat, in order to prove his worth to me - and I'm speaking about Toger, because he was in one special unit and I was in the other - I suppose it was because he wanted to prove his worth, and the Roma were asking to be forgiven and were pleading for their lives. At one point, Toger took out his knife and cut the ear of one of the Roma.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. And what happened after Toger did this, after he cut the ear of one of the Roma?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As this was happening, his uniform was all blooded over, and as I said, Maxhup hit one and the other with the baseball bat. Since he cut him - I recall this very vividly, I was a young soldier in the KLA - I was very fearful at that point, I didn't know what was going to happen, and Toger told me, "This is the way you treat the enemy and the spies." As he cut his ear, he stabbed him in his upper body a couple of times and the man fell to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You've told us about the Serb boy and one of the Roma. What -- did anything happen to the other Roma boy who was out there in the yard?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did tell you about him as well. I don't know if you understood this correctly. Maxhup beat him with the baseball bat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how many times did Maxhup beat this other Roma boy with the baseball bat?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times -- well, it's been 13 years. I really can't recall all the details and the number of times he was hit. A couple of times. Can I have a break, please, if possible?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That's fine with me. I know the witness has been feeling unwell, so that's fine with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Madam Registrar, may the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll take a break until we hear from the Registrar whether the witness is ready to resume. Court adjourned. --- Break taken at 9.49 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we ask for a closed session, I just wanted to mention to the parties that the Chamber has just received this writing from VWS, which confirms that only VWS staff was with the witness during the break and nobody else. And may the Chamber please move into closed session. If the parties want to have a look at this, they can have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. When the blinds are up, you may stand up, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Madam Kravetz, I have one clarification question. At line 17 -- at page 17, sorry, line 6 and 7, the witness answered that: "As I said, Maxhup hit one and the other with a baseball bat." We're talking about the Roma boys. And then at lines 17 and 18 you asked: "How many times did Maxhup beat this other Roma boy with a baseball bat?" Now, I'm not very clear about whether we're talking about one and the other or about one. Could you clarify that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I had seen that, Your Honour. I was going to go there. Is it okay if I ask that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Of course, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: -- I'm just going to back up a little bit in this account.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, before we speak about the beating of the two Roma, I just want to go back to the young Serb. You've told us that Ramush Haradinaj punched him with his fist a couple of times. Did anyone else of the persons that were involved in this interrogation beat or hit this young Serb?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said, it was Ramush Haradinaj. You asked me how it all started, and I said that it was Ramush Haradinaj who hit the Serb a couple of times with his fist.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm asking you if anyone else of those who were present do anything to the Serb boy, other than Ramush Haradinaj. You've already told us about Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of course the others took part in the beatings as well. I've explained clearly that it was Ramush who started it all, giving him blows with his fist, and then followed Toger. And then I clearly explained that Maxhup killed -- I mean hit one -- hit the Roma with the baseball bat. And I'm -- so when I said "the Roma," I didn't think that I needed to be more precise than that. I meant both of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, can I -- I'm sorry. Please try to listen to the questions and try to answer the question that is put to you. You are jumping about from the Serb to the Roma. You are being asked about the Serb. You told the Court that Ramush Haradinaj hit the Serb a couple of times with his fists. The question that is being put to you is: With respect to the Serb, apart from Ramush Haradinaj, was there anybody else who hit the Serb boy? We're not talking about the Roma.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that Ramush started it and the others took part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, we have heard that. Yeah. When you say "and the others took part," you are not answering the question that is being put to you. The question that is being put to you is whether anybody else hit the Serb boy? Now, instead of saying "somebody took part," you've got to say X did what or nobody did anything else to this person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for not being clear. Following in Ramush Haradinaj's footsteps, the others got involved in the mistreatments. When I say "others," I mean Toger, Maxhup, Idriz Gashi, and others who were present there. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry I can't get the answer for you, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Can I ask the question again just to follow-up from that answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You say, "Following in Ramush Haradinaj's footsteps, the others got involved in the mistreatments." In the mistreatment of whom? I'm asking specifically about the Serb boy, if anyone else was involved in the mistreatment of the Serb boy. Can you help us with that?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that after Ramush Haradinaj hit him, punched him a couple of times, he drew nearer to me. I suppose he found it demeaning to be hitting someone. And then to prove themselves to us, Toger joined, Maxhup did with the baseball bat. So the same sort of mistreatment was accorded to the Serb and then it continued with the Roma.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And just -- can you just clarify when you say "the same sort of mistreatment," what are you speaking about? Just try to explain it as best as you can.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beatings. They continued beating him and interrogating him about the whereabouts of the Serb army and their check-point.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Who continued beating the Serb boy?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Toger, as I said. It wasn't the case of, you know, you take your turn at beating him and then I'll take mine. They hit him all at once. It wasn't like they were making breaks in between.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say Toger -- I asked who continued beating him, you said Toger. What exactly did Toger do to the Serb boy?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Toger beat him. When I said "beat him," I meant punched him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Where, in what part of his body did he punch him?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All over his body.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And approximately how many times did he punch the Serb boy?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of times. I didn't keep count. Several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did any one of those present, other than Haradinaj and Toger, beat the Serb boy?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Idriz Gashi did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What did Idriz Gashi do to the Serb boy?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He dealt him blows with his fists, as did all the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, can -- I understand Your Honour wanted to have a break. I don't know if I should just continue or if we're having the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It would be preferable to have a break now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I want to go back to the incident we were discussing before the break, and I just want to let you know the reason I'm going back to it is simply to clarify or make very clear for the Judges what you saw at the time when this incident took place. So I just have some more questions in relation to that. You've told us -- we're going back to the Serb boy. You've told us that you saw Toger beat him and you said "when I say 'beat him,' I meant punch him." Did Toger do anything else to the Serb boy other than punch him?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he punched him a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes. I'm asking if in addition to punching him a couple of times --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection. Leading. Asked and answered now for about the fourth time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm just trying to clarify the answer of the witness on this point. He -- he simply -- I'm just simply trying to clarify and his answer was non-responsive. He didn't actually respond to the question. My question was whether in addition to punching him had he done anything else, and he said he punched him a couple of times. So I'm just trying to clarify did anything else happen and the witness can just say whether it did or it did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So, sir, just to go back to my question -- and I know this may seem that we are going back over and over and a bit repetitive for you but it's simply so we're clear on this. I asked you whether Toger, apart from punching the boy, did he do anything else to the boy? And you can simply respond yes or no.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did do something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Can you describe what it was that he did?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here's what he did, the same thing that happened to the -- to one of the Roma, and he did it to the Serb as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Can you be a bit more clear on that, what exactly you're referring to when you say "the same thing that happened to one of the Roma."

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did the same thing with his knife.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what was that? I know this may be difficult. I'm just trying to get you to explain to the Judges what it is that you saw him do with his knife. So just take your time.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He also took his knife and cut his ear and stabbed him in the front part of his body a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say he cut his ear, can you describe exactly the extent of the injury that he inflicted on the Serb boy, that Toger inflicted on the boy?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were injuries because he cut his ear off, and how many times he stabbed him I don't know, five times, six times. I was a freshman and I was a bit scared. I didn't keep count of the stabs, but he was injured pretty bad so he couldn't stand anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You told us earlier when I asked you if anyone other than Toger and Haradinaj had beat the Serb boy and you told us Idriz Gashi did and you said "Idriz Gashi dealt him blows with his fists, as did all the others." Can you just clarify when you say "all the others," who else you were referring to, who else beat the Serb boy?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that Maxhup and the local soldiers who were there, a couple of them, also took part because, as I told you before the break, it -- they weren't taking shifts in the beating.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What did Maxhup do to the Serb boy?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maxhup beat him with a baseball bat the same way he had beaten the Roma, and he beat him as long as he could -- he beat him until he couldn't stand anymore and fell on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Now I want to go back to an answer you gave earlier. This is on page 17, where you were referring to Maxhup and you said that "Maxhup had hit one and the other with the baseball bat." You've told us about what Maxhup did to the Serb boy. I just want to clarify when you say "one and the other with the baseball bat," who else you are referring to, just so we're clear.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Roma, they were there, the three of them. He didn't mind whom he would hit first. He beat one and then the other and then the third, and the third one being the Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And just so we're clear, when you say "he beat them," with what did he beat the two Romas?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, with a baseball bat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: For how long did this beating of the three young men take -- last?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It went for half an hour, maybe 45 minutes, because they couldn't stand being beaten anymore. They were lying on the ground. They couldn't stand.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did you or any of the soldiers who had travelled with you to Jabllanice participate in this beating?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We weren't there to beat people. We were like guests. We were there to help out, to provide escort, because they weren't -- there weren't many of them. And we didn't take part. This was all new to both me and a couple of my comrades, and we were a bit fearful.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know a name -- a man by the name of Nazmi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And who is he? Who was he?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is Maxhup's brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him while he -- while we were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And just could you be more precise, when you say while you were there, where exactly did you see him and --

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Jabllanice, in that house. While we were there, we had the opportunity to meet him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when was that, that you met him at that house in Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived on that evening and rested and maybe before Maxhup arrived, some ten minutes prior to his arrival, he introduced himself as the commander, the village commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you see -- you've told us you met him when you first arrived there in the house. Did you see him at any other time while you were there, at that house, during this first visit to Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that I may have seen him once more in that yard, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Was he in the yard when this beating and interrogation of the three young men was taking place?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the yard, but I cannot say that he took part because he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, when I asked you about what Toger did to the Serb boy, you told me that he had taken out a knife and cut his ear and stabbed him in the chest. After doing that, did Toger do anything else to the Serb boy?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but it's been a long time and I cannot remember everything. It's been 13 years, so I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. I understand. What happened after the beating stopped, what happened to the Serb boy and the two Roma boys?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After being beaten and falling on the ground, Ramush Haradinaj said, "Take them to Adem Bace in Drenica," and I can explain the meaning of that sentence. I was -- I had been in training and they taught us what that means. When somebody says, "Take them to Adem Bace in Drenica," it means: Kill them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You've -- I think I've asked you this before but just so we're clear, what does the word "Bace" mean? When you say "Adem Bace," what does the word "Bace" mean?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bace is a man who is held in high esteem by everybody and is of advanced age, and you refer to such a man as Bace. It means a highly respected man.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you know who this person, Adem, in the phrase that you've referred to, who this person Adem is or was?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. Every soldier knows that. Adem here stands for the legendary commander Adem Jashari.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know why that -- this expression, "Take them to Adem Bace in Drenica," was used?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just explained. While we were being trained in Albania, we were told that when somebody says, "Take them to Bace Adem," when your superior tells you that, it means: Go and kill them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And who told you that this was the meaning of this phrase?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told that in training in Albania. That's when we were taught that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, sir, do you know why it is that this expression was used when someone meant to -- or meant to say "kill them," why was this expression used?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a phrase and I don't know how to explain how it came about, but it -- the meaning of the phrase is killing somebody. Since Adem Jashari had already been killed at the time -- so where was Adem Jashari? He was in his grave. So, "Take them to Adem Jashari" means like take them to the grave. To my mind, that is how it came to mean what it meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And after Ramush Haradinaj said this expression, "Take them to Adem Bace in Drenica," what happened?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that the local soldiers picked up the two Roma and that young Serb, and they took them to another house which was maybe a hundred metres away. I didn't know what that house was about at the time; however, I later learned that it was a hospital and that's where they took them. And a few minutes later they told us, "Go ahead and escort the local soldiers."

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Before we move on from there, just going back, after Ramush Haradinaj said that, "Take them to Adem Bace in Drenica," did you hear anyone else of those present say anything?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that these three young boys were taken to a house, which you later learned was a hospital. Just so I'm clear, who exactly took them to that house which was a hospital?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Local soldiers from Jabllanice, that is, the villagers in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were you with those villagers when these three young men were taken to this house that you later learned was a hospital?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were told -- to be more precise, Maxhup told us that we were supposed to follow them where they were going, and that's what we did, we followed them where they went.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And where was this house that you later learned was a hospital? And I'm speaking about in which village was it?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jabllanice. It was in the same village where we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how far away you walked from the house or the compound where this interrogation and beating had taken place to get to -- just if you recall, to get to this other house that was used as the hospital?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We walked a couple of minutes. It wasn't far.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how do you know that this other house was used as a hospital?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have told you and I'm going to tell you again, I didn't know when I first heard of it. But since we were not alien [as interpreted] to the place, we were with them and we talked to the locals. And then they explained to us that there was a hospital in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if I might ask Ms. Kravetz just to clarify who it is that the witness is referring to when he says "we" at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you told us that -- you said: "But since we were not" -- I believe you meant to say "we were alien to the place" and in the transcript it appears as "not alien to the place." "We were with them and we talked to the locals. When you say "we were with them," whom are you referring to by "we"?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me and my comrades who were with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how many of you -- how many comrades were with you? When you say "my comrades," how many people are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Six, six men. As I explained at the beginning, that I was with six men. I and my six comrades who were with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how many locals were accompanying you when you were escorting these three young men?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four or five -- seven of them. I apologise. Actually, there were seven villagers and the six of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In what condition were the two Romas and the Serb boy when they were taken from the compound where the beating took place to this house that was used as a hospital in the village?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in a very poor condition or there's --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: They were in a very poor condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm sorry. Just for purposes of clarification since that seems to be what we're seeking. Is it my understanding based upon the witness's answers that there were then 13 people who accompanied the three boys to the hospital? I wonder if we could get some clarification about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I believe the witness gave that answer. It's at page 36, lines 13 to 14. It seems pretty clear, but if Your Honours consider that I need to clarify further, I'm happy to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think it's a simple -- it's a question of simple arithmetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I've always been bad at math. I was just wanting to make sure that I was right about the numbers. 13, it's clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kravetz, could you ask the witness whether he can give -- whether he knows any of the names of the seven villagers?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, do you know the names of any of the local villagers who were in that group that escorted the two Romas and the Serb boy to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was Idriz Gashi.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know the names of any other of the villagers?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You -- when I asked you in what condition the two Romas and the Serb boy were when they were taken to this house that was used as a hospital, you said it was in a very poor condition. Can you describe what you mean by that, when you say "very poor condition."

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were bloody, beaten up, that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could they still walk?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they couldn't walk.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how did these three young men make their way to the hospital if they couldn't walk?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that the local soldiers picked them up. Two of them were carrying one of these three and they basically carried them there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were the three young boys still alive when the group reached the hospital or the house that was used as a hospital?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were all still alive when they entered the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What happened once they arrived at the hospital with these three young men?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We waited outside. The local soldiers carried them in. After a quarter hour maybe, they took them out again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were the three young boys still alive when they were taken out of the hospital again?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were no longer alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I understand it's difficult to speak about this, sir, so just take your time.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I have a brief pause?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I have no objection to that, Your Honours. I'm in Your Honours' hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How brief? Do you need us to rise or do you just need to go out a short while and you come back, we wait for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's resume. It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Are you sure? We can have a break if you need it. The Judge is just simply asking you for how long you need a break, but we can have a break if you feel the need --

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five, ten minutes, if possible; if not, let's continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. If it's going to be five to ten minutes, perhaps we might just as well rise. Court adjourned. --- Break taken at 11.18 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Madam Registrar. Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Witness, before the break you told us that when these three young men were taken out of the hospital they were no longer alive. What did you do with the bodies of these three young men?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they took them out, they were on stretchers, you know, the kind of stretchers you would use for patients. They were green in colour and they were carried out on these stretchers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Who carried them out on these stretchers?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The local soldiers, the ones who took them in to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What happened after the three young boys were taken out of the hospital on these stretchers?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then they told us that we should follow the road. One of them was ahead of us, he was a soldier, a local soldier. We were just supposed to follow, so we went along.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say "we were supposed to follow," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean I, my companions, and the seven persons I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Where did you go from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went in the direction of the lake.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Which lake was that?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know what it was called at the time. I found out its name later on, and as we were walking I learned that it was Lake Radoniq and that that was where we were headed. So we didn't even know where we were headed initially until one of the local soldiers told us that we were going to a lake.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately for how long you walked from Jabllanice village to get to this lake?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: An hour and a half to two hours roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And during this walk from Jabllanice village to the lake, who was transporting the bodies of the three young boys?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The local soldiers were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And why were you and the six men who had -- who were part of your group and had travelled with you to Jabllanice in -- also part of this group escorting or accompanying the local soldiers to the lake?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were a special unit which monitored and served as escort along that trip.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you recall how it is that you got from the village of Jabllanice to that lake?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. Most of the journey took us across fields and woodland because we weren't able to take proper roads, as Serbs were present all around. So we proceeded with caution. We then reached a point where there was a canal or channel if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Can you describe that channel or canal for us?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a canal leading to the lake. I think I'm not mistaken if I say that it had steps made of concrete at its initial stages, whereas then it proceeds to a narrow canal. So if I remember correctly, there were these steps down which I suppose you'd let the water run, and at the bottom you could see mud and garbage.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What did you do when you reached this canal or channel?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We proceeded alongside the canal for some 10 metres. There was a dirt road there, it wasn't an asphalt road, and we walked along the length of this dirt road down to the lake.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you actually make it all the way to the lake or did you stop before you reached the lake?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went all the way to the lake. I remember or what I can remember of our journey on the way to the lake, we were crossing some sort of -- well, there was an amount of water there, a patch of water, and we were supposed to mind not to be seen by anyone, as there was a group of houses nearby.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you stop anywhere on this journey from the village of Jabllanice to the lake?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course we did. They -- we needed to take a rest here and there because they had to carry the bodies. We would also stop to see if there was army to be seen around. It's not like we were on our way to a wedding party. There was the army and the police, we knew that they were around.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What did you do when you reached the lake?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we reached the lake, we were, of course, told that we should surveil the area around and make sure that nobody came closer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what happened after that, after you reached the lake?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, we were making sure, keeping watch, that nobody came. On one ridge of the lake, that was where the bodies were dumped.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Who dumped the bodies there?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, the local soldiers did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know why the bodies were dumped there?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, actually, I don't. And I didn't have the authority to ask them why they had dumped the bodies there. It wasn't down to me to ask that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did anyone who was part of this group explain to you why it is that you went all the way to the lake to dump the bodies?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well -- well, there was no need to put that question, and of course, bodies do decompose and there was a village nearby and here was the lake and, you know, where would you dump a body?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: After the bodies were dumped there, what happened?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We headed back. When we returned, one of the local soldiers - and of course we were talking amongst ourselves - told me that there was one other spot where it was dumped the same way. He showed me that spot and then we returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say "there was one other spot where it was dumped the same way," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me make this clear. As we were on our way back to the village, we took the same route. So as we were heading back, the dirt road was on our right-hand side and this stream was on our -- or the river was on the left-hand side. Some 300 or 400 metres into our journey, he started telling me that this wasn't the only spot where they would dump them, there was several other spots as well, and this was to our left, some 2- or 300 metres beyond lake where they were dumped into the canal. So now as we head toward the lake it's on our right-hand side, but as we were heading back from the lake to the village, he said that it was to our left.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say "this wasn't the only spot where they would dump them," what are you referring to by "dump them"? What was dumped there?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you so, the bodies. So we're starting from scratch again. As we were surveying the terrain, the bodies were dumped into the lake. And some 200 metres into our journey back, we started making conversation, as anybody would, and they told us that on our left -- to our left, where the river was, and as we were heading back to Jabllanice, it was on the left bank of the river, that bodies had been dumped as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And who would dump bodies there as well in this other location that you've explained?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't down to me to ask that. He said, "We dumped them." That was the -- what the local soldier said, but he didn't name any names. And of course it wasn't down to me to just put that question to him and ask him, "Well, why don't you tell me now who was it who dumped the bodies?"

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. After you dumped the bodies at this location what happened?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I just explained to you that we returned and that on our way back, in our conversation he told me that the bodies had previously been dumped to our left as we were heading back. It was to the left of that concrete canal, that's what he told me. And then we returned to the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: To which village did you return?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And once you were back at Jabllanice, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We rested a while and headed for our zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So do I understand correctly, you left the village?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you leave that same day?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on that same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Just going back a little bit, when you told us that Ramush Haradinaj had given this order of "take them to Adem Bace in Drenica" and you left the compound, what happened with Mr. Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's not Adem Bace, it's Bace Adem Jashari, just to make sure. I didn't see Ramush again, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What about Mr. Lahi Brahimaj, did you see him again?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went along with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say "they went along with him," whom are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Toger and Maxhup.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And they went where?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't follow them to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, yesterday when we were talking about when you first arrived in Jabllanice village to this house that you've described in the compound, you said you were taken down to the basement and you saw other persons being held there. Do you know what happened to these other persons who were held there?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I never saw them again, so I don't know what happened to them, if you mean the elderly people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to the persons other than the Serb boy and the two Roma that you've spoken about.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that because I never saw them again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know who was in charge of this house that you visited in the compound with the basement where these persons were held?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. It was Maxhup as the one in charge, because when I say "Maxhup," I meant that he was the host being of that village. So it was only natural that he should be the one in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know why it is that this Serb boy and the two Romas were interrogated and beaten in the way that you've described?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know -- well, it wasn't just this once that they interrogated people. It is normal for people when they are captured to be interrogated about the whereabouts of the enemy forces, about the location of their check-point, and such-like. Well, at least I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And why do you say it's normal when people are captured to be interrogated about these things?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you want to learn as much as you can about the enemy when you're a soldier, when you're a commander, you want to learn more to make sure that your people are not ambushed and trapped, and that's normal and natural for every war. It is natural that you would ask people to tell you where their forces are. When you're a soldier, you want very much to know where your enemy is, you want to know which route to take, which direction you can expect an attack to come from.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were these Roma and the Serb boy that you saw interrogated and beaten in uniform at the time that you witnessed this incident?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who exactly do you mean? I apologise. I didn't understand well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I meant the young Serb and the two Roma, when you saw them during this beating and interrogation, were they in any sort of uniform?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, civilians, just as I am now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we take the break could we briefly go into private session just for a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. Yes, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us about your first trip to the village of Jabllanice. Did you go there a second time in 1998?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that I would like to go back to something, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, sir, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a bit of stage fright for lack of a better word. This is the first time I've appeared before a Court. I apologise to both you and the Trial Chamber for mixing up units, because I was mentioning only Tigers, Tigers this, Tigers that, and it wasn't really that way. I can tell about our unit, what it was called, and about theirs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could go into private session for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. Yes, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us about your first trip to the village of Jabllanice and I had asked you when we started if you had gone there a second time in 1998.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went there a second time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: How much time or how much later after this first trip to Jabllanice did your second trip take place?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three weeks later, possibly a little more than that. I don't really remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did you travel there alone or did you travel there with other people?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With others.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: With how many other people did you travel there and who were these persons?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- I travelled with those same companions of mine. We belonged to the same unit, and wherever we went, we went together.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: At what time of the day did you arrive in Jabllanice village?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was early in the morning. In the early hours of the morning we arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Why did you travel to Jabllanice village a second time?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were ordered by the commander to go there and help them out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say "by the commander," which -- without mentioning any names, just so you can tell me if you're speaking of your commander or some other commander.

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What did you do after you arrived in the Jabllanice on this second occasion?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to the same house as the first time around, and clearly we met Maxhup there, had a talk, and rested a while because it wasn't such a short journey after all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You say that you had a talk with Maxhup. What did you discuss, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spoke about how we travelled, whether we saw enemy units anywhere, and -- it was a normal conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: After you finished resting, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, Maxhup told us that we were to escort two Roma and a Serb again to a neighbouring village, that we should take them there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And where were these two Roma and the Serb that you were to escort, where were they?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the basement of the same room where that previous group had been.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say "that previous group," which previous group are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The young folks about whom I spoke today, the two Roma, the Serb youth, and the two older people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you go down into that basement?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what happened after Maxhup told you that you were to escort these two Roma and the Serb to another village?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The local soldiers from Jabllanice village brought them out. We -- or they handed them over to us. And when we went there for the second time, Maxhup and the local soldiers had captured a Pinzgauer vehicle from the Serb army, and they gave us that vehicle to travel where we could use it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know whether anyone else was -- I'm speaking about the second visit that you made to Jabllanice. Do you know whether there was anyone else being held in that basement other than these two Roma and the Serb that you're speaking about?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I don't know about you, but I can only speak about things in the sequence in which I remember them and I will tell you what I remember. I don't remember, however, whether anybody else was there. I haven't seen anybody because I didn't go into the basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: For how long did you remain in Jabllanice at this house on this second visit?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of hours, three, four hours maybe.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you told us earlier this morning that during your first visit there, you witnessed an interrogation and beating of a Serb youth and two Roma boys. During this second visit, did you see anyone being questioned by the soldiers in Jabllanice or by anyone else?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. No. There were no interrogations. We were only required to take them to the neighbouring village.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you take these three individuals, the Serb and the two Roma, to the neighbouring village?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And why did you have to take them there?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I couldn't say. When you're a soldier, you can't ask the commander why you are to do this or that. You're ordered to help out somebody and that's what you do, and when you're told, "Take them to another place," then you go there. You're not meant to ask why or how when you're a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And after you took these three individuals to the neighbouring village, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're rushing with your questions a bit, if I may say. I would like to finish what I was speaking about. While we were taking there, one of the Roma who spoke Albanian -- I heard one of them calling the other by his name. I remember that the name was Afrim, that was the name of one of the Roma.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And approximately how old were these three individuals that you were escorting?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the same age as the others, possibly a bit younger. I've already explained to you it wasn't up to me to ask them their age or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you know why these three individuals were being held there at this house -- at this basement in Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I apologise. I was a soldier, and let me explain you again. I had no right to ask any questions why they were here, how they were brought here, why they were taken prisoner. It wasn't for me to ask. It was my duty to carry out my task and return to my unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you escort these three individuals on your own or did anyone else come with you?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I and my companions who were with me and one more local soldier who knew the way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And after you had escorted these three individuals to this neighbouring village, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As usual, we returned to our zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: During this second visit, did you -- you've told us you met and spoke with Maxhup. Did you see anyone else there at this house in Jabllanice during the second visit, other than Maxhup?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw local soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were these three persons that you escorted, I'm talking about the Serb and the Roma, dressed in any kind of uniform?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us that after you escorted these three individuals you returned to your zone. Did you visit the village of Jabllanice on another occasion, on a third occasion?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went there again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kravetz, before you go into the third visit, could I ask the witness whether he knows the name of the local soldier that went with the six of them to escort the three people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now you're -- you were telling us that you went to the village of Jabllanice on a third occasion. When did this third visit to Jabllanice take place, approximately how much later than the second visit?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A month or a month and a half possibly elapsed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And again, sir, did you travel there on your own or with other people?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I travelled with the same companions as on the first two occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And why did you go there a third time, to the village of Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've explained to you that we went there to help out because we were from the neighbouring zone. The Dukagjini Zone and the Drenica Zone are next to each other. When we needed help they came to us and when they needed help we went to them, and that's why we went there, to help them out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what did you do when you arrived in the village of Jabllanice on this third occasion?

utterances.speaker: 81 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third time when I went there I arrived at the same house and had a rest for a while. After that I saw Maxhup again, not just me, of course, but I and my companions. And after a short conversation about how we were, how we had travelled and so on, he took us to the basement to see who was in there. There were two young Serbs. One was rather tall, the other less so. If I'm not mistaken, one of them had blond hair and wore a uniform, if I'm not mistaken. But I think he did wear a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Can you describe this uniform this person with the blond hair was wearing, just as best as you remember.
